passages.note: Prime-sponsor record of a digital-impersonation civil-liability bill; not a platform-removal/labeling/moderation measure.

passages.provision_quote: A provider of an interactive computer service may not be subject to an action for DIGITAL IMPERSONATION for PUBLISHING INFORMATION that is provided by another information content provider.
passages.note: Enacted text creates a private right of action against the impersonation's publisher, not a platform-removal/labeling mandate, and expressly exempts interactive computer service providers.
House Final Reading was 57-0-3-0-0, with zero No votes, so the vote alone cannot carry a chair even apart from the subject-matter mismatch.

rows.reasoning: HB2394 (2024), which Kolodin prime-sponsored, signed into law 2024-05-21, and voted Y on in the House Final Reading (57-0-3-0-0), creates a private civil cause of action against persons who publish a deceptive AI-generated 'digital impersonation' of a candidate or other person, while providing that 'a provider of an interactive computer service may not be subject to an action for digital impersonation for publishing information that is provided by another information content provider.' It does not require platforms to remove or label content, encourage voluntary industry standards, or address government involvement in content-moderation decisions, so no passage establishes any rung of the misinformation ladder.
